assessment.note: Three NHANES-based estimates of the share of the US population 2+ consuming pizza on any given day: 11% (2017-2020), 11% (restated), 13% (2007-2010). Same underlying survey instrument; the 13%→11% drift is a real decline, not a contradiction. These are the core prevalence inputs for the per-capita route.
All three give ~6% for adults 60+, from the same NHANES family. Consistent age gradient; useful for age-structuring Chicago's population but not independent of p1.
Age-split prevalence: children ~14-20%, adults ~10-11%. Consistent with the overall 11-13% and the 6% elderly figure. Same survey source.
Source-of-pizza shares: restaurant 56%, grocery 26%, school 12%, other 6%. p7 restates the 6% 'other'. These partition the channel mix and are needed to split restaurant vs at-home mass.
Occasion shares (dinner/lunch/snack) for adults and children, from the same USDA report. Internally consistent; used only for context, not a direct mass driver.
Mean energy from pizza per consuming day: 538 kcal (children), 744 kcal (adults). These are the key bridge from prevalence to mass via an energy-density conversion.
Share of pizza consumed at home (59% overall, 65% adults, 49% children). Older vintage (2007-2010) but consistent with the 26% grocery + home-prepared framing; used as a cross-check on channel split.

All from one Rentech Digital listing scrape of Chicago pizza restaurants (1,987 outlets, April 2026). Internally consistent (914+1073=1987; 1848+139=1987). Single source, so not independent confirmation, but the outlet count is the best available for the transaction route.

All from the same Technomic/IFMA Top 500 report: LSR pizza units, AUVs, chain sales, and food-away inflation. One underlying dataset; used together for the sales-based route, not as independent checks.
US frozen pizza retail sales ~$7.2-7.3B (Circana/IMARC) and private label ~$1.1B. Consistent magnitudes; used to size the at-home/frozen channel.
Census-based Chicago city population ~2.75M (2025) and Cook County ~5.2M. Same source (Census via Tribune). The city figure is the pinned denominator; county is context only.

Market-intelo deep-dish market report: $0.9B global deep-dish market, 65% Illinois/Chicago, occasion splits, and 58.3M visitors with 35-45% seeking deep-dish. Single low-quality vendor report; internally consistent but weak provenance. Used only as a soft cross-check / visitor adjustment, not a primary driver.
Technomic pizza-chain growth (0.5% vs 3% overall) and Giordano's/Lou Malnati's store counts. Consistent slow-growth picture; used for trend context only.

August 2026 CPI components (food at home 2.2%, away 3.4%, limited-service 3.2%, cheese, flour, produce). Same BLS-derived source; used to deflate/convert 2024-2025 dollar figures to 2026 and to note price-driven substitution.

NHANES 1-day recall gives 11% consuming on any given day, while Technomic reports 35% weekly consumption in 2025. Not a true contradiction: 'any given day' vs 'any given week' differ by ~7x, and the weekly figure rose from 24% (2022). The weekly rate implies a higher daily prevalence than the 2017-2020 NHANES figure, suggesting possible understatement of 2026 prevalence; treat as a range, not a conflict to resolve.

13% (2007-2010) vs 11% (2017-2020) same metric — a genuine decline over time, not a measurement conflict. Supports using the more recent 11% as the base with a possible upward adjustment for 2026 given p80.

Grips 'Chicago Food Specialties' AOV ($100-200) and Marketintelo deep-dish market ($0.9B) are different scopes (online specialty orders vs global deep-dish restaurant revenue) and cannot be reconciled directly; both are weak-provenance and used only as loose bounds.

The best computed estimate is 1,027,630 t/day (80% model-based interval 574,883 to 1,836,936 t/day) for the city of Chicago proper, averaged over calendar year 2026, counting pizza mass as sold or served. The single method (weight 100%) multiplies Chicago population 2,750,000 people by daily pizza prevalence 11 percent of population, blends adult and child energy intake 744 kilocalories and 538 kilocalories using adult share 0.78, divides by energy density 250 to get mass, and applies a Chicago multiplier 1.15.
